name: session_shell
description: Persistent pty-backed bash — all calls share one long-lived shell attached to a real TTY. Unlike `bash`, this supports interactive commands: `ssh host` keeps you logged in across calls (next `ls` runs remotely), `python3` drops you into the REPL, `read -p` parks on stdin. `cd`, `export`, aliases, functions persist. Return rule is unified: exit_code captured when bash reaches its prompt; otherwise returned when output idles for ~1.5s (interactive process waiting for input); hard cap at `timeout`s which passes Ctrl-C through the pty. Set `reset=true` to kill and restart, clearing all state. Not for long-running background processes — use `bash(run_in_background=true)` for those.

command.description: Shell command (or input for whatever subprocess currently owns the pty, e.g. a line to type into a python REPL after `python3` was launched in an earlier call).

timeout.description: Hard total-time cap in seconds (default 60). On expiry ^C is sent through the pty to the foreground process group; the shell remains alive.

idle_threshold.description: Seconds of output-idle that count as 'command done waiting for input' (default 1.5). Shorter = faster return for interactive commands; longer = more room for slow-streaming output. Most callers leave this unset.

reset.description: If true, kill and restart the persistent shell before running anything, clearing cwd, env, aliases, and any subprocess state (e.g. you were stuck inside an ssh session). Default false.
